definition: Software that automatically displays or downloads advertising material when a user is online, often bundled with free programs and designed to generate revenue through ad impressions.
metaDescription: Learn about adware - unwanted software that displays ads on your device. Understand how it works, why it matters for privacy, and how to protect yourself.
simpleExplanation: Adware is software that shows you unwanted advertisements, usually pop-ups or banners, while you use your computer or phone. It often comes hidden inside free programs you download and can slow down your device while tracking your browsing habits.
whyItMatters: Adware compromises your privacy by tracking your online behavior, collecting personal data for targeted advertising, and potentially exposing you to malicious ads. It can slow down your device and create security vulnerabilities.
technicalDetail: Adware operates by injecting advertisements into web pages, displaying pop-up windows, or redirecting browsers to advertising sites. It often uses browser extensions, system-level hooks, or proxy settings to intercept and modify web traffic, while collecting user data through cookies, tracking pixels, and browsing history monitoring.

examples.explanation: You download a free PDF reader that secretly installs adware, which then displays pop-up ads every time you browse the internet, even when not using the PDF program.
Adware changes your browser's homepage and search engine without permission, redirecting searches to advertising-heavy sites while collecting data about your search habits.
A mobile game displays excessive banner ads and pop-ups that interrupt gameplay while secretly tracking your app usage and location data to sell to advertisers.
